lead.headline: Anthropic will sell shares at $70 to $78 each in a Nasdaq listing that could value it at up to $1.3 trillion
lead.short: Anthropic said it will sell its shares at between $70 and $78 each when it lists on New York's Nasdaq exchange, raising up to $64bn. That would value the Claude maker at between $1.1tn and $1.3 trillion, below the $2tn some backers predicted in summer. Its shares, under the ticker ANT, are due to start trading on 19 November.

why.text: It is the first listing of a leading AI model maker, and investors will read it as a verdict on the whole AI boom.

more: Anthropic aims to sell 825 million shares, according to its filing with the US Securities and Exchange Commission. Seven tech companies including Google, Nvidia, AMD and Microsoft have agreed to buy $26bn of shares; most are investors in Anthropic or major suppliers of its computing power. Its revenue for the six months to June rose to $16.2bn from $1.1bn a year earlier, though it is still loss-making.

Bankers are preparing to lift the valuation to $1.5tn or more after strong investor demand, the Financial Times reported. The offering falls short of SpaceX's record $86bn listing in June. "There are three massive companies that investors have wanted to be part of for the last three years and that's SpaceX for sure, Anthropic is next, and perhaps next year OpenAI," said Art Hogan of B. Riley Wealth Management.

update.new: Anthropic sets its price range and listing date.
update.front: The price is set: the biggest AI listing yet starts trading on 19 November.

seconds.headline: The US charges three Iran-backed men over a string of plots in Europe and the US, including one at Britain's RAF Fairford
seconds.short: The US Justice Department has charged three Iran-backed operatives over a series of plots in the US and Europe, including a major incident in September near RAF Fairford, a British base used by US forces. One, a dual Iranian-Iraqi national, is accused of directing contacts in Britain from a New York prison where he awaits trial on earlier charges.

why.text: It ties Iran directly to attacks on Western soil just as Washington says the war is winding down.

more: The indictment, unsealed on Tuesday, names Iranian Mohsen Mohajeri, Iraqi Mohammad Ali al-Hassani and Mohammad Baqer Saad Dawood al-Saadi, who holds both nationalities. It says they planned attacks in Europe under the name of a new group, HAYI. "Of the 18 terrorist attacks in the spring of 2026 for which HAYI claimed responsibility in Europe, seven took place in the UK," the department said.

FBI director Kash Patel said the men were involved in nearly 20 attempted attacks in support of Iran's Revolutionary Guards and the Iraqi militia Kataib Hezbollah, and that one "allegedly sent coded messages to assist in future acts of violence" from detention. Seven men have been arrested in Britain over the Fairford incident, and the US moved its bombers out of the base last month. Iran denies any involvement.

facts.charged: Mohsen Mohajeri, Mohammad Ali al-Hassani, Mohammad Baqer Saad Dawood al-Saadi

update.new: The US charges three Iran-backed men over the plots, including Fairford.
update.front: For the first time, a government has charged named men with running Iran's attacks in Europe.

seconds.headline: Indian shares hit an eight-month high as foreign investors return, then give back part of the gain
seconds.short: The Sensex jumped 1,097 points in early trade on Wednesday and the Nifty rose more than 1%, to their highest levels since 27 February, as cheaper oil and a cooling of the AI trade drew foreign money back. By 1.48pm profit booking had trimmed the gains, with the Sensex up 0.73% at 81,697.99.

why.text: Foreign investors spent two years leaving India for AI stocks, and their return is now driving the market.

more: The Sensex and Nifty have gained 10.5% and 10% in November, on course for their best month since November 2020, while MSCI's emerging markets index is down 1.2%. Foreign portfolio investors have bought $5.68bn of Indian shares this month, their biggest monthly purchase since September 2024. Jefferies joined HSBC and Citi in turning bullish on Indian equities on Wednesday.

Banks led the rise, with HDFC Bank up more than 2% and Axis Bank and State Bank of India about 3% each, while IT and real estate shares turned lower in the afternoon. AI-related stocks such as Netweb and E2E Networks rose up to 9% on Anthropic's listing plans. Brent fell to a two-month low of $89.16 a barrel on Tuesday.

update.new: An eight-month high on foreign buying.
update.front: Foreign money is back in Indian shares after a two-year exodus.

seconds.headline: Hardik Pandya leaves Mumbai Indians for Punjab Kings, and Arshdeep Singh goes the other way in a straight swap
seconds.short: Mumbai Indians captain Hardik Pandya will join Punjab Kings, and Arshdeep Singh, India's leading wicket-taker in T20 internationals, will move to Mumbai, in a trade completed ahead of IPL 2027. Pandya moves at a fee of ₹18 crore, up from ₹16.35 crore, while Arshdeep joins Mumbai at his existing fee of ₹18 crore.

why.text: Mumbai lose their captain and Punjab their all-time leading wicket-taker before the auction.

more: Pandya won four IPL titles with Mumbai, in 2015, 2017, 2019 and 2020, before moving to Gujarat Titans ahead of IPL 2022 as captain. His second stint at Mumbai, where he first arrived in 2015, now ends.

Arshdeep moves after eight seasons with Punjab, where he made his IPL debut in 2019. With 111 wickets in 96 IPL matches, he is the franchise's all-time leading wicket-taker; he took 21 wickets in 2025 and 14 in 2026. His ability to take early wickets with the new ball and to bowl under pressure at the death will add depth to Mumbai's attack, the IPL said. He is with India's one-day side in New Zealand.

stories.headline: A tanker carrying six Indian seafarers is hit by a projectile in the Gulf, and one Indian is among four crew injured
stories.short: The Liberia-flagged supertanker MT Fujairah Energy, with six Indian seafarers aboard, was hit by a projectile on Tuesday while sailing through the Gulf from Al Ruwais to Dubai, Shipping Minister Sarbananda Sonowal said. Four crew members were hurt, including one Indian, who suffered minor injuries and has been taken ashore for a medical examination.

why.text: Thousands of Indian sailors crew Gulf shipping, and attacks there are rising even as the US talks of the war ending.

more: "The remaining 18 crew members, including the other 5 Indian seafarers, are safe and accounted for," Sonowal said, adding that the government was in close contact with the ship's managers. Thirty-seven ships were attacked in the Strait of Hormuz and nearby waters in October, the most in any month since the war began, according to the Washington Institute for Near East Policy, and 10 so far in November.

Iran's Revolutionary Guards Navy said two tankers caught fire on Tuesday after hitting naval mines on an "unauthorized route" in the strait. Brent crude rose 0.78% to $92.20 a barrel early on Wednesday, after a two-month low, as the attacks blunted hopes for a truce.

update.new: A tanker with six Indians aboard is hit, and attacks on shipping hit a record.

stories.headline: Firecrackers caused more than 80% of Delhi's pollution the day after Diwali, a government institute estimates
stories.short: Emissions from fireworks made up more than 80% of Delhi's pollution load on Monday, the day after Diwali, according to estimates by the Indian Institute of Tropical Meteorology. A separate IITM assessment put firecrackers at 71.1% of the city's PM2.5 between 1am and 9am on 9 November, against 5.6% at the same hours on 7 November.

why.text: It settles, with the government's own numbers, how much of Delhi's worst night came from one evening of fireworks.

more: PM2.5 at Jahangirpuri reached 4,985 micrograms per cubic metre at 3am on 9 November, The Times of India reported, though the Delhi Pollution Control Committee later revised the data. Vehicle exhaust made up only 6.9% of PM2.5 in that window. Delhi's AQI was 308, "very poor", on Wednesday morning, and stronger winds are expected to bring relief.

In Lucknow on Wednesday, Uttar Pradesh's chief minister defended the fireworks. "If pollution occurred, it would be mitigated as well. No problem," he said. "Nobody says anything to those who polluted the entire system with their corrupt misdeeds. But if the public burst crackers one day, it created pollution!" His government imposed no restrictions.

update.new: An IITM estimate pins most of the spike on firecrackers.

briefs.text: The locomotive and five coaches came off the track at Digaru station in Kamrup (Metro) at about 6.54am on Wednesday. Northeast Frontier Railway said all passengers were safe and continued on another train.

stories.headline: The House blocks the bid to impeach Pete Hegseth by 211 votes to 204, and Trump hails his 'exoneration'
stories.short: The House of Representatives voted 211 to 204 on Tuesday to send articles of impeachment against Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth to the Judiciary Committee, in effect killing the effort for now. Thomas Massie, who brought them, was the only Republican to vote against the referral. Hegseth called the bid a "farce" and "sabotage".

why.text: Republicans have closed ranks on the war for now, but Democrats can revive the charges when they take over in January.

more: More than a dozen members, including 11 Democrats, missed the vote. Trump wrote on Truth Social that the effort had "miserably FAILED" and called the result the "EXONERATION of a Great American Patriot", citing "Victories in Venezuela and Iran". Hegseth spoke at his first news briefing at the Pentagon in six months.

Massie had said he hoped to push Trump to replace Hegseth while Republicans could still confirm a successor quickly. Impeachment resolutions can be carried past the end of a congressional term, so Democrats, who take control of both chambers in January, would be able to take the matter up next year.

briefs.headline: Nine members of the Kennedy family sue to block Trump's planned 250-foot arch near Arlington National Cemetery
briefs.text: The nine say the 250ft arch would block the view of John F Kennedy's grave and those of thousands of veterans. A judge has paused work for 14 days, and the White House called the suit "unfortunate".

briefs.text: The 41-year-old, described as a "senior soldier, entrusted with sensitive information", is held in London. FBI director Kash Patel said the case "involves allegations of espionage, which is of the utmost concern".

briefs.text: It is the second month above 1,000. The one flaw used before a fix, an Outlook spoofing bug, scored only 6.5 out of 10; "Maybe we should just go home," said watchTowr's Jake Knott.

briefs.headline: GTA 6 will be playable on the old Xbox One at launch on 19 November, but only by streaming it from the cloud
briefs.text: Game Pass subscribers can stream GTA 6 through Xbox Cloud Gaming from 1am ET on 19 November, the launch day, Rockstar said in a post on how the game runs on current consoles.

stories.headline: Mauricio Pochettino wants the Manchester United job, and United are finalising a deal in case they sack Michael Carrick
stories.short: Mauricio Pochettino, the US men's national team coach, is interested in moving to Manchester United, and the interest is mutual, multiple sources told The Guardian. United, expected to sack Michael Carrick after their worst start to a season in four decades, are finalising a deal for the Argentinian should Carrick go, according to reports.

why.text: United would be hiring a coach with Premier League experience in mid-season, and the US would lose theirs before a World Cup cycle.

more: His contract with US Soccer, extended through 2030, has a release clause of about $10m (£7.5m), a figure that rises if United keep his staff, including his long-time assistant Jesús Pérez. Pochettino took the job in 2024 and led the US to the last 16 of the 2026 World Cup, by most accounts a disappointment.

"Every time we sign a contract, it's to go to the last day of the contract," Pochettino said after his renewal, before adding: "In life, nothing is sure. Less in football." The US play Haiti in the Concacaf Nations League in Cincinnati and Miami in the coming days, and Pochettino is due to speak to reporters on Friday.

briefs.headline: Scott McTominay reveals he had his heart shocked in hospital two days before Scotland's World Cup opener
briefs.text: The Napoli midfielder was sedated for the procedure two days before the Haiti match in June, when his absence was put down to a stomach complaint. He had surgery for an irregular heartbeat in September.

briefs.headline: Endrick says José Mourinho calls him every day but does not rule out a loan away from Real Madrid in January
briefs.text: "I am only 20, so I will see how things develop," the Brazilian said. "Every day he contacts me, not to discuss football, but to inquire about my personal life."

briefs.text: Conway is recovering from concussion after colliding with Matt Henry in training, and Ravindra dislocated his shoulder filming a diving catch in September. Tom Latham captains; the first Test starts in Wellington next week.

briefs.text: The average was 148.67 on Diwali and 248 the next day. The Nagar Nigam station recorded the worst reading, 294 on 9 November.

briefs.text: BTech students Diya Dutta and Kashish Jadhav built the prototype under Dr Surya Prakash; it changes size with a scissor-like mechanism. A patent application is in process.
